source_read: PDF pp. 1689-1690 and the unnumbered third page (PDFs/MDMA/Halvorsen_2021_BenchmarkingChallenges.pdf): text extraction and rendered p. 1689 for paragraph counts; MAPP1 figures checked on its publisher page in my own tab. Step 1 not run this round.

design.note: Matters Arising letter without data; the editors' narrative-review checklist is the protocol's choice where no commentary design exists.

key_findings.note: p. 1689, 1st and 2nd paragraphs (seven running-text paragraphs in all: six on p. 1689, one on p. 1690).
Every SMD and interval as printed, with references 4, 5 and 6 as the card assigns them.
The letter's text calls reference 8 a meta-analysis of CBT for PTSD; only the reference title (adult anxiety disorders) suggests a wider scope.
Recomputed: 3 x 90 + 3 x 480 + 9 x 90 = 2,520 minutes = 28 x 90 = 42 x 60.

reporting_issues.note: Right that the remission figures come from other populations and definitions, but the letter itself describes reference 8 as a meta-analysis of CBT for PTSD (4th paragraph); 'across anxiety disorders' is an inference from the reference title (Springer et al., 2018), and whether the 53% is a PTSD subset cannot be checked without that meta-analysis. The same wording is in the card's analysis and selection_effects fields. The sharper problem, which the card records under selective reporting, is that the letter sets other trials' remission or loss of diagnosis against MAPP1's strictest outcome (remission, 33% of completers) rather than its loss of diagnosis (67%).

instrument.note: Editors' narrative-review checklist, stored as none-applicable.

domains.note: None of the 10 references is by the three authors.

domains.domain: Balance of evidence on how MDMA-assisted therapy compares with first-line psychotherapies

overall.note: High, following the two high domains.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: the comparative statements rest on cross-trial figures against different controls and on MAPP1's strictest outcome. The 12-word quotation in the claimed field is verbatim.

missed: The letter says the cost-effectiveness of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy had not yet been formally evaluated (6th paragraph), yet MAPP1 itself cites a 2020 cost-effectiveness analysis (its reference 11: Marseille, Kahn, Yazar-Klosinski and Doblin, PLoS ONE), and the reply says a phase 3-based evaluation was under review. Relevant to cl_mdma_ptsd_cost.

Resick et al.'s 22.2% and 17.5% still meeting criteria correspond to 77.8% and 82.5% without the diagnosis at long-term follow-up in an intent-to-treat sample (editors' arithmetic), which the letter sets against MAPP1's completers' remission; the like-for-like MAPP1 figure is loss of diagnosis, 61% of the dosed MDMA arm (editors' calculation).
